Where this sits

Every recommendation passes one global filtering gate, whatever the channel or use case. The funnel below measures it.

The guardrail funnel

One central gate, applied once

Four layers, applied once and centrally — so every team surfaces the same right, consented researchers instead of re-filtering or missing a rule. Click a layer for its rules.

Impact on the current recommender

Same pattern in both samples: strong candidates in, only ~a third reaches a contactable person — lost to data, not the model. All four layers applied.

Where the audience goes, layer by layer

LayerSample A keptSample B kept
Activity & quality78.8%83.8%

Contactable53.0%51.6%

~Half are lost at the final layer, mostly for no email on record (A −2,164; B −1,072).

Bottom line: the model isn’t the bottleneck — contact data is. With all four layers applied, ~a third of surfaced candidates is contactable. Best levers: email coverage, de-duplication, and repairing the activity join. Report yield as contactable candidates, not raw count.

1 · The funnel — four cuts

Order changes attribution, not the result — every cut is an AND, so the final population is identical. Running Active first means identity drops 1,833,696 instead of tens of millions, since unaffiliated single-paper profiles are already gone.

Appendix · method

Every figure comes from a query in the accompanying SQL file — nothing estimated or carried over. Rules with no data are marked unmeasurable, not dropped.

  • All AIRAK reads are the load of 14 August 2026. The table is rebuilt in place rather than versioned, so figures move slightly between loads: this load is 526,643 rows larger than the one used in the first draft of this deck, a change of 0.35%.
  • Exclusion codes are read from the status_reason table, which holds every code against a researcher — not from researcher_availability.primary_reason_code, which keeps only the highest-priority one and would undercount every rule except the top one.
  • No Loop-to-AIRA cross-walk is involved anywhere in this deck. Every rule, and both samples, are keyed on the AIRA author id directly, which removes the usual risk of matching the wrong person.

3 · The two samples 4
SampleBaseActiveEligibleIdentifiedContactableSurvives
Sample A · Research Topics12,85910,4899,6057,5614,00931.2%
Sample B · Reviewers4,9774,2573,9103,3451,72734.7%
  • The samples are recommender output, not a population: Sample A is every candidate retrieved for five Research Topics, Sample B every candidate retrieved for five manuscripts. They answer a different question from the Universe funnel — not "how many researchers could we contact" but "how much of what the pipeline hands an editor is usable".
  • Sample A counts candidate rows, not people. A researcher retrieved for two topics counts twice: 12,859 rows against 12,809 distinct researchers. Sample B is de-duplicated within each manuscript: 4,977 rows, 4,975 distinct. The row is the unit of work, so the row is the base.
  • The candidate ids were joined to the rule flags with a single parameterised BigQuery query over the 17,750 distinct ids across both samples, then the cuts were applied in order. No candidate was dropped by the join.
  • 293 Sample A rows and 91 Sample B rows have no record in AIRAK at all. They are carried through and fail at the Active cut — with no AIRAK profile they have no publications on record, so they register as not currently publishing.
  • Source is the retrieval channel, from the sample files — in_profiles/in_publications in Sample A, Channels Found In in Sample B — not a rule computed in BigQuery. Sample A skews toward the publications database (7,859 of 12,859 candidates); Sample B is retrieved evenly by construction (2,477 from each channel, plus 23 found in both). In both samples the researcher-profile channel converts to Contactable at a noticeably higher rate than the publications channel: 38.2% vs 26.4% in Sample A, 37.2% vs 32.3% in Sample B — profile-sourced candidates are more likely to have a usable email on file.
4 · Rules that cannot be measured 4
RuleStatus
Unsubscribed for Research Topic communicationNo code exists for it in the 22-code dictionary. Not applied.
Deceased · RetiredAuthor.IsDeceased and Author.IsRetired are empty on every row. The dictionary carries codes ADC and ARD, but nothing is written against them. Not applied.
Marked as out of office in DEONot in BigQuery in any form: no code in the dictionary, and person.user_status only holds Activated, Non-Activated and Deleted. The deck shows the DEO screen count of 938, which counts current editorial roles, not people — one editor can hold several. Shown for information, never deducted.
No verified email (code ANV)Unusable: it only ever appears alongside another exclusion, so relying on it would report almost no email problems. Email coverage is measured from address validity in AuthorEmail instead.
5 · Conventions, and how to read the percentages 6
  • The board is interactive; these appendix figures are the baseline. Every number here is the all-rules-on, all-sources view. On the sample tabs you can untick any rule, filter to a single retrieval source, click a funnel bar to see the specific rules that dropped each stage's candidates, and export that dropped list to CSV — the funnel, tables and drop counts all recompute live from the same candidate data.
  • Every percentage is against the population entering that cut, never against the Universe, unless the line says otherwise. This is why the same rule shows a different percentage on different tabs — the base has changed, not the count.
  • Rules overlap, so individual counts never sum to the combined drop. A researcher with no affiliation and no last name is dropped once. The Combined row is the honest total; the rows above it are each independent.
  • Order changes the attribution, not the destination. Each cut is an AND over the same rule set, so the final population is the same whichever order they run in. Applying the Active cut first means the identity cut drops 1,833,696 rather than tens of millions, because the profiles it would have caught are already gone.
  • Arithmetic verified at every stage. Universe funnel: 152,027,513 − 141,874,898 = 10,152,615; − 910,355 = 9,242,260; − 1,833,696 = 7,408,564; − 3,806,658 = 3,601,906. Sample A: 12,859 − 2,370 = 10,489; − 884 = 9,605; − 2,044 = 7,561; − 3,552 = 4,009. Sample B: 4,977 − 720 = 4,257; − 347 = 3,910; − 565 = 3,345; − 1,618 = 1,727.
  • The Universe is context, not a denominator. It includes every author record ever ingested, most of which are single-paper profiles with no affiliation. Coverage rates quoted against it will always look small and mean little.
